stem: Which of the following describes all solutions to the inequality \(-2 < x + 3 \le 7\)?
solution: Subtract 3 from all three parts: \(-2 - 3 < x \le 7 - 3\).
So \(-5 < x \le 4\). The signs stay the same because nothing was multiplied or divided by a negative number.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This subtracts 3 from the left part only and leaves the right part unchanged.
explanation.B: Correct. Subtracting 3 from every part gives \(-5 < x \le 4\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This adds 3 to each part instead of subtracting 3.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This switches which end is included: \(-5\) is not a solution (the left inequality is strict), but 4 is.
